length.sourceNote: Cited on Wikipedia to a 1945-dated page on timelapse.dk describing the pistol as a roughly 12-inch cylinder; that site did not respond when checked, so the figure is recorded as estimated rather than verified.

barrelLength.sourceNote: From the Wikipedia infobox, uncited there (3.25 in). This is the vented barrel and expansion chamber inside the suppressor housing, not a conventional exposed barrel.

effectiveRange.sourceNote: From the Wikipedia infobox, uncited there: 25 yd stated for daylight use; a separate 7–8 yd figure is given for night use, and the manual states the pistol was most effective fired in contact with the target.

capacity.sourceNote: From the Wikipedia infobox, uncited there. The primary production chambering (Mk II / IIA).

From the Wikipedia infobox, uncited there. A later variant (the 9mm Mk I) developed after reported poor field results with the .32 ACP version; the standard 9mm loading is supersonic, so the ported barrel had a larger job to do bringing it below the speed of sound.
